scope: DISTRIBUTED_CLOSURE_CLAUDE_LANE_C_OWNERSHIP -- Asia, Africa, Middle East, multinational/regional programs, and multilateral/cross-region treaty queues not naturally anchored in Lane A (Americas + Oceania, closed by Codex, 57/57) or Lane B (Europe, reserved for Gemini, unpublished at time of this manifest).
exclusion_method: Of the 161 canonical REMAINING identities (152 existing_program + 2 missing_program + 7 treaty_queue): Lane A (Codex) territory = Argentina, Australia, Bahamas, Barbados, Brazil, Canada, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, Guatemala, Guyana, Jamaica, Mexico, New Zealand, Panama, Peru, Trinidad & Tobago, United States, Uruguay -- all 57 already CLOSED by Codex Lane A (DISTRIBUTED_CLOSURE_CODEX_LANE_A_OWNERSHIP.json / DISTRIBUTED_CLOSURE_CODEX_LANE_A.md, lane_total_closed=57). Lane B (Gemini, reserved, not yet published) territory = Albania, Austria, Belarus, Belgium, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Montenegro, Netherlands, North Macedonia, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Serbia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, United Kingdom, plus the European Union and Nordic Region entities (41 existing/missing items) and 4 explicitly European-anchored treaty queues (UK_BILATERAL_AND_CONVENTION_RECONCILIATION, FRANCE_BILATERAL_LIST_RECONCILIATION, EUROPEAN_CONVENTION_PARTICIPANTS_AND_VERSIONS, EURIMAGES_MEMBERSHIP_AND_ELIGIBILITY -- Eurimages is a Council of Europe fund).

explicit_gaps_not_claimed_by_lane_c.reason_not_claimed: Oceania/Pacific -- geographically contiguous with Lane A's Australia/New Zealand claim, but NOT itself among Codex's 57 claimed identities. Not Asia/Africa/Middle East/multinational per Lane C's own scope definition. Flagged as an unclaimed cross-lane gap rather than silently absorbed into Lane C's denominator or silently dropped.

Naturally anchored in Lane A's Oceania geography (Australia). Codex Lane A explicitly left lane_treaty_start=0, so this remains formally unclaimed by any lane as of this manifest -- flagged as a gap, not claimed by Lane C, since it is not Asia/Africa/Middle East/multinational.
Naturally anchored in Lane A's Americas geography (Canada). Same reasoning as the Australia queue above -- flagged as a gap, not claimed by Lane C.
Naturally anchored in Lane B's European geography (United Kingdom). Reserved for Gemini Lane B, not claimed here.
Naturally anchored in Lane B's European geography (France). Reserved for Gemini Lane B, not claimed here.
Explicitly European multilateral framework (Council of Europe CETS 147/220). Reserved for Gemini Lane B, not claimed here.
Council of Europe co-production support fund, administered from and predominantly membered by European states. Reserved for Gemini Lane B, not claimed here.

ibermedia_inclusion_rationale: IBERMEDIA_MEMBERSHIP_AND_FRAMEWORK is claimed by Lane C, NOT Lane A or B, because it is genuinely cross-region -- the Ibero-American Programme spans Spain and Portugal (Lane B geography) AND the large majority of its member states across Latin America (Lane A geography), with the coordinating secretariat (SEGIB) itself headquartered in Madrid but representing a 22-member multinational bloc, not a single country's bilateral pathway. This matches Lane C's explicit brief: cross-region partner-list queues not naturally anchored in Lane A or B, and multinational or regional funding programs.
